[#hash-password-hashing-compare]
.What each of "Password hashing" is
[cols="2,1,3,2,1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Output | Security | Standard | Status | In the browser (WebCrypto)

| <<hash-argon2id,`argon2id`>>
| 16 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| each guess costs its memory and passes, on a GPU too
| RFC 9106, one lane
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2d`>>
| 4 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| the strongest against trade-offs, open to side channels on a shared machine
| RFC 9106, every parameter
| where no attacker shares the machine
| no

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2i`>>
| 4 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| weaker than Argon2id against trade-offs of time and memory
| RFC 9106, every parameter
| legacy
| no

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2id`>>
| 4 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| each guess costs its memory and passes, on a GPU too
| RFC 9106, every parameter
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-scrypt,`scrypt`>>
| 1 to (2^32 - 1) times 32 bytes
| each guess costs 128 r N bytes of memory
| RFC 7914
| recommended
| no
|===

[#hash-password-hashing-choose]
.How to choose among "Password hashing"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-argon2id,`argon2id`>>
| 38.3 ms (sodium)
| 39,690 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP's first choice for password storage]; link:https://www.password-hashing.net/[the Password Hashing Competition's winner]; link:https://bitwarden.com/help/kdf-algorithms/[Bitwarden's vault key, as an option]
| Storing passwords and deriving keys from them.

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2d`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106[RFC 9106's variant where no attacker shares the machine, such as proof of work]
| Never for passwords; only where a format names Argon2d and no attacker shares the machine.

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2i`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106[RFC 9106's variant for side channels alone, which it does not recommend over Argon2id]
| Only where a format names Argon2i; Argon2id for anything new.

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2id`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106[RFC 9106's recommended variant, with its parameters p, K and X]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP's first choice for password storage]
| Passwords with a pepper, several lanes or associated data, or a format that fixes them; otherwise the function argon2id.

| <<hash-scrypt,`scrypt`>>
| 19.1 ms (sodium)
| 29,540 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/data-structures-and-encoding/web3-secret-storage/[Ethereum's keystore files (Web3 Secret Storage)]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP: N 2^17, r 8, p 1 when Argon2id is not available]
| When a format demands scrypt; otherwise Argon2id.
|===

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's, a reference measured on 2026-11-16 on Apple M5 Max that decides nothing: the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target.
